citations.name: requirements.sdk.graph.criteria.deterministic_procedures
citations.commentary:
A criterion can also compute its answer with deterministic Rust code.
Its `ValidationContext` exposes the [inspection operations](validation-context.md)
used by the agent's graph tools.
[Searches and outlines](validation-context.md#find-a-node-then-read-its-contents)
help locate code to inspect; tracked reads and edge selections record input
identities and fingerprints, so changes to those inputs can invalidate the
resulting evidence.

rationale:
The commentary block in `md/requirements/sdk/graph/criteria.md` (the `{cite}` fence for `deterministic_procedures`) is explanatory prose. Its claims agree with the cited declarations, and every citation uses the `cite` role, which suits commentary.

- **Deterministic criteria.** The claim that a criterion can compute its answer with deterministic Rust code restates `requirements.sdk.graph.criteria.deterministic_procedures`. That requirement says execution can use tracked inputs and needs no configured agent.
- **Shared context.** The claim that `ValidationContext` exposes the inspection operations the agent's graph tools use matches `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.shared_context`. That requirement says direct reads and reads served by the agent tools record inputs in the same `ValidationContext`. The linked section "Find a node, then read its contents" exists in `validation-context.md`.
- **Search and outline.** The claim that searches and outlines help locate code to inspect is supported by `requirements.sdk.graph.search.search_text.behavior` and `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.outline_source.behavior`. The first describes finding matches with paths and excerpts. The second describes inspecting a file's selectable items so they can be read.
- **Staleness.** The claim that tracked reads and edge selections record input identities and fingerprints, so changes can invalidate the evidence, is supported by `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.inputs` and `requirements.sdk.graph.evidence.checking_records`. The first keeps observed dependencies, including node identities and edge labels, with the output. The second compares each saved fingerprint with current state.

No claim contradicts a cited declaration. None of the citations also appears as `{impl}` or `{test}` on this item, so none is redundant.

text: :::{req} deterministic_procedures
`Criterion::execute` can compute an answer without a configured model provider.
A criterion can compute its answer directly using tracked inputs; deterministic
execution needs no configured agent.
:::{req} shared_context
During one call to `verify`, direct reads by the criterion and
reads served by the SDK's agent tools record inputs in the same
`ValidationContext`. For example, if criterion code reads a test and the agent
then reads its helper, both node fingerprints accompany the returned answer.
A subsequent verification starts with an empty dependency list.
:::{req} search_text.behavior
`TextMatches` is `SearchResults<TextMatch>`. Each match contains a project-relative
file path, a line number, and the excerpt. `complete` reports whether the search
returned all matches under {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.provider_results.search_completeness`.
The tool returns the page ID, completeness flag, and tagged regular-expression
matches with their paths, line numbers, and excerpts. `context_lines` adds surrounding lines to
each excerpt and defaults to zero. `limit` bounds the number of matches.
For example, `search_text({"pattern":"invalid selector","prefix":"src"})`
finds occurrences of that phrase under `src/`.
:::{req} outline_source.behavior
`Sources::parse` reads a single file snapshot. `OutlineContent` retains its
identity and parsed contents under {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.provider_results.parse_snapshot`.
Inspect the selectable items in a visible project file. Pass a returned selector
and the same `path` to `read_source` to read that item. Follow [`next`](#continuing-a-paged-result) to see more items.
:::{req} inputs
Keeps a typed output with its source, criterion, version, and observed dependencies. `output` borrows the answer and `into_output` consumes the wrapper.
`verify` constructs this value from the criterion's completed answer and
execution trace. `load_evidence` reconstructs it from the selected saved record.
Its node identities and edge labels keep their domain-defined types.
```rust,ignore
pub struct Fingerprinted<D: Domain, O> { /* private fields */ }
impl<D: Domain, O> Fingerprinted<D, O> {
pub fn source_node_id(&self) -> &D::NodeId;
pub fn criterion_path(&self) -> &CriterionPath;
pub fn version(&self) -> Option<&CriterionVersion>;
pub fn dependencies(&self) -> &[Dependency<D::NodeId, D::EdgeLabel>];
pub fn output(&self) -> &O;
pub fn into_output(self) -> O;
:::{req} checking_records
```rust,ignore
/// Compare each recorded input with the current domain state.
/// Return true when every fingerprint still matches, including an empty trace.
pub fn check_inputs<D: Domain, O>(
domain: &D,
inputs: &Fingerprinted<D, O>,
) -> Result<bool, D::Error>;
The function resolves the recorded dependencies through graph operations and
fingerprinting, comparing each with its saved observation. A fingerprint
mismatch returns `Ok(false)` and permits an early return; it need not resolve
later dependencies. An encountered dependency-resolution failure returns an
error.
The function observes the current state that the caller intends to inspect.
Freshness checking has a separate observation scope from criterion execution.
Checked observations enter the new trace when execution explicitly reads
or delivers them.
A checked snapshot can be reused if it still represents the current state.
::::{definition} application_domain
:phrase: application domain
:::{cite} requirements.sdk.domain
An *application domain* is the application's graph, node contents, and evidence
storage, made available together for criterion execution. In the SDK, it
implements [`Domain`](../rustdocs/trust_but_verify/domain/trait.Domain.html) to supply
its shared types, node and edge operations, and evidence persistence.
:::{definition} criterion
:phrase: criterion
A *criterion* is a value describing a test to perform on a
{term}`requirements.sdk.graph.node`.
In the SDK, its type implements
[`Criterion<D>`](../../../rustdocs/trust_but_verify/graph/trait.Criterion.html) for the
{term}`requirements.sdk.application_domain`. Its
members describe the question's answer, identity, review rules, and execution.
:::{definition} source_node
:phrase: source node
A *source node* is the {term}`requirements.sdk.graph.node` on which a
{term}`requirements.sdk.graph.criteria.criterion` is evaluated, identified by
[`Criterion::source_node_id`](../../../rustdocs/trust_but_verify/graph/trait.Criterion.html#tymethod.source_node_id).
Tracked reads of its own contents or those of other nodes can supply inputs
without changing the criterion's source node.
:::{definition} node
:phrase: graph node
A *graph node* is a thing identified in the application's graph, such as a
requirement, a function, a test, or an issue. The application's
[`Domain::NodeId`](../../rustdocs/trust_but_verify/domain/trait.Domain.html#associatedtype.NodeId)
identifies it; its contents and the criteria evaluated on it are separate from
that identity.
